changes.change: new: path- and package-based Java tracking classifier
new: positive and negative classifier cases; the real repository tracks exactly the runtime; generated Java and classes stay ignored
`git ls-files *.java` empty  ->  no tracking-policy violation (7 assertions)
implementation must be recoverable (archived or tracked at the commit); no excluded root except the empty runs/.gitkeep; no committed secret; a tampered tracked blob is detected
recovery completeness over archived + tracked files; no committed secret

tracked files listed with git blob ids (tracked_at_commit) and secret-scanned (create refuses on a committed secret); restore verifies them against the commit tree; agents/skills counted over archive + commit; tracked_files_intact allows exactly the recorded modifications; the excluded-path check reads the archive
fresh-clone fix: the placeholder-section edit matches CRLF as well as LF (a Windows checkout holds CRLF; the edit silently did nothing)
fresh-clone fix: `bmad dry-run --mode MOCK` is refused as a usage error before the run is loaded, so the result no longer depends on local run records

new: `* text=auto eol=lf`. A Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true wrote every text file with CRLF, changing the SHA-256 of hash-bound evidence (authorization manifest, reverse artifacts, BMad pin and bindings) and voiding the LGA records in a fresh clone; checkouts now reproduce the committed bytes
fresh-clone fix: the archived-entry tamper case runs only when the archive has entries (a pristine clone has no uncommitted file); the tracked-file tamper case always runs

weakened_assertions: none: every replaced assertion still fails on any generated or unexpected tracked Java, every backup check still runs, and new negative checks were added
